subject: Private deployment maintenance kickoff — pinning, windows, rollback checklist
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

Subject: Private deployment maintenance kickoff — pinning, windows, rollback checklist

Hi team —

Thanks for agreeing to a controlled maintenance window for your Private deployment. This thread will be the working thread for finalizing the plan; I’ve attached a short preflight checklist. High-level proposal:

- Version pin: pin to release v2028.04.1 for the control-plane and v2028.04.0+rev for inference nodes.
- Maintenance window: Sat 2028-04-20 02:00–06:00 PDT (4 hours). We recommend a 2-hour canary followed by full-fleet rollout.
- Rollback: automated rollback script + manual bailout criteria (service error-rate > 1% for 10 minutes or KV cache mismatch detected).
- Canary: 2 dedicated nodes in your VPC with traffic routed at 5% for 30–60 minutes.

Preflight items we’ll run 48–72 hours prior: node health sweep, backup of KV cache snapshots, snapshot of pinned model artifacts, and load-replay smoke tests. See attached preflight-checklist.csv.

Questions for you before we lock the window:
1) Confirm the Sat window works for your ops team and any downstream batch jobs to avoid collisions.
2) Are you comfortable with the pin set above (control-plane + inference variants) or do you need a different exact build SHA pinned?
3) Any additional firewall/VPC egress windows that need to be scheduled?

I’m copying Priyom and Marissa for rollback/playbook items and Vivek for network draining steps. If we agree, we’ll share the maintenance notice draft for your customer-facing comms.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Marcus —

Thanks for the summary. A few clarifying items from our side:
- The proposed window looks fine, though our analytics batch finishes at 01:45 PDT; 02:00 start is OK but we’d prefer no unexpected restarts during the 02:00–03:00 timeframe.
- On pinning: we’d like exact build SHAs for both control-plane and model artifacts. We use artifact immutability to match our audit requirements. Can you provide those SHAs when you have them?
- KV cache: if you snapshot and restore, how do you guarantee TTL/consistency for keys created post-snapshot? We want to avoid cache-induced inference drift.

Also looping in our SRE consultant — they’ll want to review the rollback criteria.

—Alex
Alex Chen

On Tue, Apr 10, 2028 at 09:12 AM Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com> wrote:
> High-level proposal:
> - Version pin: pin to release v2028.04.1 for the control-plane and v2028.04.0+rev for inference nodes.

Alex — quick answers and an operational proposal:

1) SHAs: we’ll publish the exact artifact SHAs in the runbook within 24 hours (will include the tarball SHA and model artifact digest). We will lock the pin in the deployment manifest 48 hours before the window and publish an immutable manifest to the Drive link below.

2) KV cache approach: we do NOT attempt to backfill keys created after snapshot. The plan is:
   - Pause write paths to the cache cluster during the brief snapshot window (30s drain) using a leader-fencing signal.
   - Capture a TTL-aware snapshot with metadata (creation timestamps).
   - On restore, keys older than the snapshot point are restored; writes post-snapshot are preserved on active nodes and reconciled via a short replay step.
   - If key-level reconciliation fails, our fallback is to expire caches and allow rebuilds (this is safe but increases latency temporarily).

3) Rollback automation and manual bailouts:
   - rollback-script.sh (attached) will attempt an automated rollback to the pinned manifest.
   - Manual bailout: runbook page PRIV-4521 lists decision gates (error-rate, tail-latency, model-response divergence). If any gate trips, we execute immediate traffic cutback to 0% and initiate rollback.

4) Canary: propose 5% traffic for 45 minutes; health checks include 95th p99 latencies, error-rate, and a prompt-set quality check (we’ll run the 20 prompt regression set live).

Drive runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDEF_runbooks_private (will add SHAs and exact manifests).

I’ll be on the call for the maintenance kickoff and will own the rollback execution with Vivek.

—Priyom
Priyom Das

Alex / Marcus / team —

Thanks for the details. A couple product/contract notes from my side:
- Customer comms: I’ve drafted a maintenance-notice-draft.docx with minimal customer-facing language and an opt-out timeframe (48 hours). If you want, we can remove the technical specifics and post only the window and expected impact.
- SLA impacts: since this is a scheduled maintenance with 72h advanced notice, our standard policy is no SLA credit, but if there’s an extended outage >30 minutes we’ll evaluate a one-time service credit. We’ll document this in the runbook and the notice.
- Billing/usage: any megatoken-count inconsistencies caused by cache rebuild should be flagged in telemetry and we'll reconcile.

I’ll send the finalized customer notice once the window and pins are locked.

Best,
Marissa Cole
